newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Ahold plans supermarkets in China - paper.
newsitem.headline: Ahold plans supermarkets in China - paper.

text.p: Dutch supermarkets group Ahold NV is planning to set up a supermarket chain in China, in a joint venture with a local company, newspaper de Volkskrant said on Saturday.
Ahold expects to establish the 50:50 joint venture with China Venturetech Investment Corp (CVIC) by the end of next week, the paper said, quoting a spokesman.
The cost to Ahold will be between 100 million and 200 million guilders.
In the last two months, Ahold has invested in joint ventures in Thailand and Malaysia and has said it has bold plans for expansion in Asia.
In August, the company said it planned to push into China by opening its first store in or near Shanghai by the end of the year. It said it planned to work with a local partner.
